title: Jude Bellingham set for Madrid derby return, Kylian Mbappe ‘100 per cent’ fit
content:
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham is available to return for Sunday’s La Liga fixture against Atletico Madrid after being sidelined for seven weeks with a hamstring injury, Alvaro Arbeloa has confirmed.

The Real Madrid head coach also insisted forward Kylian Mbappe is back to full fitness for the weekend’s Madrid derby, having made his comeback from nearly one month out with a knee injury as a substitute during Tuesday’s Champions League win over Manchester City.

Bellingham has not featured since the victory over Rayo Vallecano on February 2, and was named in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for March’s international break on Friday. The Athletic reported on March 6 that Madrid sources considered the Madrid derby as a more realistic return date for the 22-year-old.

“He (Bellingham) is available now; he’ll be in the squad tomorrow,” Arbeloa told a press conference on Saturday. “We’ll see if he plays; I think he will. He’s available, and I’m really looking forward to seeing him on the pitch.”

Bellingham’s absence has resulted in an increase in minutes for 18-year-old midfielder Thiago Pitarch in recent weeks. Arbeloa said the teenager should still get first-team opportunities despite Bellingham’s return.

“Having Bellingham back is excellent,” the Madrid head coach added. “The fact that Thiago has managed to perform at this level is also excellent news. I love these problems; it’s a blessed problem to have to choose between these two players. They can play together too; it doesn’t mean that just because Bellingham is back, Thiago has to stop playing.”

Mbappe, meanwhile, was named in the France squad for March’s friendlies against Brazil and Colombia, having featured for the final 21 minutes of Tuesday’s win at the Etihad. The France forward has had two spells out with a knee injury this season, and Arbeloa said he would “definitely be playing” against Atletico.

“I told you, the day he returns is because he’s 100 per cent,” Arbeloa said of Mbappe’s condition. “In Manchester we saw two or three bursts of pace he made and in every move he showed he’s in great shape. Maximum confidence, assurance and excitement at having such a game-changing player back. And at 100 per cent.”
